🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Charles F. Porter, the actor who played NASCAR pioneer Wendell Scott in the 2011 ESPN movie Wendell Scott: A Race Story, has died at 47 after a long battle with cancer.

Porter died on Monday, November 2, 2026, at his home in Calabasas, California, his wife, Candice Tab-Porter, confirmed to USA Today. His family also confirmed the news to The Hollywood Reporter. Porter had battled Hodgkin lymphoma, first diagnosed 17 years ago.

Born March 13, 1979, in Oxford, England, Porter played defensive end at Duke University before a back injury led him to acting. He moved to Los Angeles in 2002 and built a career on both sides of the camera, with television roles on House, Bones, Without a Trace, The Parkers and Close to Home, and film roles including Johnny Was and Peppermint.

He was best known for starring as Wendell Scott, the first Black driver to win a NASCAR Cup race, in the 2011 ESPN film. Behind the camera, Porter founded Black Bench Productions and produced the 2025 Lifetime movie Finding Faith, along with A Miracle Before Christmas and Christmas Angel for BET+. He also published three books.

Rest in Peace, Charles F. Porter.

Sources: USA Today; Entertainment Weekly; The Hollywood Reporter.
